messages.text: which session in my main mj instance is 47a5ea02 ?

1. fix messaging to use/display the session names we use in the TUI session list, seems like sometimes it works mostly it doesn't, i assume it must be divergent code from TUI; in fact have a subagent search for session names and make sure we're DRYed across the codebase

2. a session name I set manually should take priority over autogenerated names

3. TUI never picked up a generated name for 5fd9ecf4cf4d217d5baa0a2248addf4f, not sure if our bug or claud's

The first implementer finished less than a fifth of the change, and it did not compile or test anything. I closed it and started a second child to finish the work. This one is the more capable "subtle" type and starts from the partial edits.

**What the partial change already does (I read the diff):**
- **New-session fix, item 3:** `actions.rs` now saves a manual name only when the caller sent a title. Sessions started from the web or phone will now show the generated name. The change is correct but not tested yet.
- **Message names:** `deliver_session_message` now uses the sender's TUI name, shortened to its first line and at most 80 characters.
- **Old helper:** `display_title()` is now private, and its callers outside `mj-core` use `listed_title()`.

**What the new child still has to do:**
- Use the live name in child questions, child reports, `list_agents` and spawn results, with the ID kept beside it.
- Merge the copies of the notice-name helper into one.
- Replace dashboard labels that show only a short ID.
- Check whether the web viewer always sends a title.
- Make the rename box in the web viewer start with the same name the TUI shows.
- Add the tests, then run the build, clippy and the tests of the changed crates.

I also told it to check the meaning of each migrated caller, especially `go.rs`. It must also keep old child-report records readable, because those records are saved and replayed.

Still open for you: whether to clear the default-text names on the 13 existing sessions so their generated titles show.

Waiting on the new child.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The first change shows why a working tree should be read before you trust a report. "Made private and migrated callers" took 25 changed lines, while the list of call sites still to change has about 40 entries.
- Old child reports can still be read back from storage. That is why the brief says to add a new name field instead of reusing `task_name`: old records must still load.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

> whether to clear the default-text names on the 13 existing sessions so their generated titles show

i want to show generated titles over defaults, yes, but "default > generated" is the wrong rule in the first place?

No, "default > generated" is not the rule, and the code doesn't use it. The rule in `listed_title()` (`mj-core/src/state.rs:2087`) is: **manual name > generated name > creation title.** The "X via Y" default is the creation title, so it already comes after the generated name.

The bug was in the stored data. The web New action saved the default text in the manual-name field, `session_title_override` (`server_runtime/actions.rs:179-186`). So for those 13 sessions, the system correctly applied "manual beats generated", but the manual name was really the default. The code fix stops this for new sessions. It can't repair the existing ones, because their stored value looks exactly like a rename you made yourself. That's why they need a one-time data fix.

**Planned data fix:** a one-time store migration. It clears the manual name only where all of these are true:
- it equals the session's creation title;
- that title is exactly `"{project or bundle} via {profile_id}"`, the output of `default_session_title()` (`state.rs:2989`);
- the session was not created as a sub-agent. A sub-agent's manual name is set on purpose to its `task_name`.

After that, those sessions show their generated title, or the creation title if none was generated. The one real case it would wrongly clear is a rename you typed that exactly matches the default. That seems unlikely. It would also be a one-time change, not a rule applied every time a name is read.

I'll assign the migration once the current implementer finishes, so only one child writes to the store code at a time. It will include a test for the clearing conditions.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- A repair at read time, such as "ignore a manual name that looks like the default", would put a guess into the naming rule forever. A one-time migration fixes the bad data once and keeps the rule simple.
- Sub-agents must be excluded because their spawn code (`controller/subagents.rs:474,491`) sets both `title` and the manual name to `task_name`. Without the default-pattern check and that exclusion, the migration would clear those names too.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
good, that's what i want, ty

Confirmed: I'll add the migration once the current implementer finishes, then review both changes together before I commit.

Waiting on the implementer now.
tell it to run targeted tests only

I sent the instruction. The child is busy, so the message is queued and it will read it at its next tool call. It will now run only the new and changed tests, plus existing tests for the code it edited, chosen by module or test name. It still runs clippy on the crates it changes, and it will list the exact test commands in its report.

Waiting on the implementer.

The naming change is finished but not committed. It touches 34 files. Clippy and `cargo fmt` are clean, and the new and changed tests pass. What it does:

- **One rule:** `display_title()` is deleted. Every name now comes from one function, `listed_session_title`, which uses the manual name, then the generated name, then the creation title.
- **Agent text:** messages and child questions use that name, shortened to one line of at most 80 characters.
- **Child reports, `list_agents` and spawn results:** they show the child's live name, with its ID kept beside it. Old saved reports still load, because the new name field is optional.
- **Web viewer:** the rename box now starts with the same name the TUI shows. The fix in `actions.rs` from before is unchanged.
- **Dashboard labels:** most job labels that showed only a short ID now use the session name. Two in `startup_prompts.rs` are not done yet.

**Test failures:**
- `termination_pty` `first_startup_discovers_both_agents…` failed once while the machine was busy, then passed on rerun. It is likely a flaky test, but that is not proven.
- One JS test fails because Playwright is not installed on this machine.

I started two children, and they work on separate files:
1. **Migration:** a one-time store migration that applies the rule you approved. It also fixes the two remaining labels in `startup_prompts.rs`. It will count the matching sessions in the live store with read-only queries only, and it runs only targeted tests.
2. **Review:** a read-only check of the naming change. It looks for call sites whose meaning changed and for compatibility problems between versions. One I want checked: the implementer renamed a field (`InPlaceSubagent.task_name` became `name`), and that may break a daemon and worker on different versions if the struct is sent between them. It also checks that control characters in titles cannot reach agent text, and that the new tests would fail on the old code.

After both report, I'll review the combined diff and commit. I won't push without asking.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `listed_session_title` takes the raw columns instead of a whole session record. Code that reads straight from SQL, such as `usage_report.rs`, can then use the same rule instead of keeping its own `COALESCE` copy, which is how the naming paths fell out of step before.
- Saving the child's name as an optional field lets new and old versions read each other's records, so no protocol version change is needed. Renaming a field that is sent between processes does not have that property, which is why the review checks `InPlaceSubagent`.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Waiting on both children.

I'm waiting on two things: the mj-core tests running in the background, and the migration child.

**What the review found (no correctness or compatibility problems):**
- The order of names is right everywhere. `go.rs` numbering and the setup refusal keep their meaning.
- `InPlaceSubagent` is never serialized. It only builds a prompt inside the controller, so renaming its field is safe.
- The new fields `child_name`, `given_title` and the `name` in `list_agents` are optional additions, so older versions can still read the data.
- The new tests fail on the old code, so they check the new behaviour.

**What I fixed myself:**
- **Control characters (P2, confirmed):** the creation title is stored exactly as typed. A terminal escape sequence in it could pass through `bounded_one_line` into agent message headers. `bounded_one_line` (`mj-core/src/state.rs:3060`) now first removes terminal controls, using the same cleaner that `normalize_session_title` uses. I added a test for an OSC 52 escape sequence.
- **A second copy of the bounding rule (P3):** `safe_subagent_name` (`mj-core/src/subagent.rs:1322`) now calls `bounded_one_line` and only adds its own angle-bracket escaping. One small side effect: a long sub-agent name is now cut at a word boundary instead of at an exact character.

**Two places that still do not use the TUI name. Your call:**
1. **SessionWiki index (`sessionwiki.rs:664`).** For a session with no name yet, the index uses the first user message, such as "Investigate X", instead of the default "project via claude". This is how it worked before, not something the change broke. I recommend leaving it, because the first message is more useful for searching old sessions. It is a second naming rule, though, so tell me if you want it removed.
2. **Archive and restore (`checkpoint/latched.rs:170`, `sessionwiki.rs:2113`, `daemon/state.rs:291,296`).** These save the creation title, and a restore then saves it again as a manual name. So a renamed session comes back with its creation title as a fixed name, and that name hides any later generated title. It is the same kind of bug as the web New action. I left it out because it changes what restore does with saved records. I recommend fixing it as a separate follow-up: save `listed_title()`, and on restore set the manual name only if the session had one. Tell me if you want it in this commit instead.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The control-character gap was there because only some names were cleaned. Manual names and generated names pass through `normalize_session_title` when they are saved. The creation title does not, so the cleaning has to happen when the name is shaped for display.
- Bugs 2 and 3 have one shared cause: one field, `session_title_override`, means "a name a person chose", but several places also use it to pin a name the system chose.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The mj-core tests for my two fixes pass: 86 tests in the `state::tests` and `subagent` modules, including the new control-character check.

Still waiting on the migration child. You haven't decided the two open questions yet, so I'm not changing those parts:
- the SessionWiki index naming;
- whether archive and restore go in this commit or a separate follow-up.

The migration child found that the exact rule matches only 4 of the 13 sessions, and `5fd9ecf4` is not one of them. The inputs to the default title change after a session is created, so comparing against the current values misses most rows:
- **Managed clones:** `project_directory` becomes a clone path. For `5fd9ecf4` the last part of the path is the clone ID, not `mjolnir`.
- **Move:** moving a session changes its profile. For example, `sm-watch via claude3` now has profile `claude`.
- **Bundle renames:** `bifrost` became `bifrost-history`.
- The original creation profile is not stored anywhere.

**What I decided, and sent back to the child:** match the shape of the default title instead of rebuilding it. The migration will clear the manual name only when all of these are true:
- the manual name is exactly equal to the creation title;
- the session is not a sub-agent;
- the title is exactly `<word> via <word>`, where each side has no spaces and " via " appears only once.

This still keeps typed web titles such as "Fix the parser", renames that differ from the creation title, and sub-agent names. The tradeoff: if you once typed a title or rename that is exactly two single words joined by "via", it would also be cleared. I think that is unlikely, and it fits what you asked for: generated titles over defaults. The child will rerun the read-only check against the live store and list any match beyond the 13 sessions.

The rest of the migration child's work is done:
- **Migration 111:** one transaction. The compatibility floor stays at 110, because older versions already accept an empty manual name. It runs before the daemon loads its state.
- **`startup_prompts.rs`:** its job labels now use the session name.
- **Tests:** the schema tests (34), the `startup_prompts` tests (4) and clippy all pass.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The migration cannot rebuild the default title because the session record keeps only current values, not the values from creation. That makes the "X via Y" shape the only evidence still in the store.
- Keeping the compatibility floor at 110 means an older `mj` binary can still open the migrated store. The migration only sets a column that can already be empty to empty, which old code already handles.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Waiting on the child's rerun. After that I'll review the combined diff and commit. Two questions are still open for you: the SessionWiki index naming, and whether archive and restore go in this commit or a follow-up.
